official.deadline_note: Two-stage deadline: the application must first be submitted in the OSIRIS Application system by 31 January 2027 23:59 CET, and must then be complete by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET. Incomplete applications will not be considered for the scholarship selection. Final decisions are communicated by Student Life and International Mobility before mid-April 2027 (date subject to change).
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 academic year - applications for the English-taught Master's programmes starting 1 September 2027
official.status_note: The official page is live for the 2027/2028 round: a maximum of 26 Radboud Scholarships are available, allocated as Faculty of Arts (2), Faculty of Law (2), Nijmegen School of Management (5), Faculty of Philosophy, Theology and Religious Studies (1), Faculty of Science (9), Faculty of Social Sciences (7).
official.tuition_coverage_note: A Radboud Scholarship will reduce your tuition fee to EUR 2,771.- (amount to be confirmed). For example: a grant holder in 2027/2028 will pay a tuition fee of only EUR 2,771.- instead of EUR 19,000 (depending on your programme).
benefits: A Radboud Scholarship will reduce your tuition fee to EUR 2,771.- (amount to be confirmed); a 2027/2028 grant holder pays EUR 2,771.- instead of EUR 19,000 (depending on your programme)

Meet the English language proficiency requirement for the Master's programme of your choice

Proof of English proficiency for the Master's programme of your choice
selection_criteria: Academic excellence: outstanding study results in your present field of study (for example grades, test scores, publications), relevancy of your previous degree to the Master's programme, and the ranking of the university where you obtained your previous degree(s)

Ambition: quality and relevance of your motivation letter for the Master's programme, promise based on previous achievements, performances and work in the relevant field, and life experience and/or extracurricular activities such as internships or volunteering
References: quality of the recommendations in the two reference letters, preferably two academic references

All applicants are individually considered by the selection committee of the faculty they applied to; faculties may base their selection on other criteria as well, and some study programmes hold interviews
coverage: Reduction of the tuition fee to EUR 2,771.- (amount to be confirmed), against an illustrative full fee of EUR 19,000 for 2027/2028 depending on the programme
The costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are NOT covered by the scholarship
application_method: Indicate during your application for admission to a Master's programme in the OSIRIS Application system that you wish to apply for a Radboud Scholarship
Upload three additional documents requested by the system: two reference letters and a curriculum vitae
If you already uploaded these documents for the Master's programme application, you can upload the same documents again for the scholarship application
Selection for the scholarship and admission to the Master's programme are two separate processes; admission does not imply selection for the scholarship
official.application_route: Apply for admission to an English-taught Radboud Master's in the OSIRIS Application system, tick the option that you wish to apply for a Radboud Scholarship, and upload two reference letters plus a CV.
official.study_mode: Full-time (full-time enrolment at Radboud University is a condition of the award)
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EU/non-EEA passport holders only, and you must not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is specifically for talented, highly motivated non-EEA students from all non-EU/non-EEA countries; a maximum of 26 scholarships are available for 2027/2028
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any English-taught Radboud Master's programme, except Erasmus Mundus Master's programmes and joint-degree Master's programmes. Awards are allocated per faculty: Faculty of Arts (2), Faculty of Law (2), Nijmegen School of Management (5), Faculty of Philosophy, Theology and Religious Studies (1), Faculty of Science (9), Faculty of Social Sciences (7).
official.duration: Nominal duration of the Master's programme (the second year of a two-year programme is conditional on passing all first-year courses)
official.description: The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a very selective scholarship programme that offers talented, highly motivated, non-EEA students with outstanding study results the opportunity to be awarded a scholarship for a complete English-taught Radboud University Master's programme. It is a partial scholarship funded by the Profiling Fund of Radboud University: it reduces tuition to the statutory rate and covers visa, residence permit, health and liability insurance, while the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered.
official.region: Europe - Netherlands (Nijmegen); open to all non-EU/non-EEA countries
official.program_type: Partial scholarship (tuition-fee reduction plus visa, residence permit, health and liability insurance), merit-based, funded from the Profiling Fund of Radboud University
official.english_requirement: You must meet the English language proficiency requirement for the Master's programme of your choice; the university sets and publishes the accepted minimum test scores per programme rather than one scholarship-wide score, and recommends submitting proof of English proficiency before the 14 February 2027 deadline.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a tuition-fee surgery award, not a living allowance: Radboud cuts your non-EEA fee to the statutory rate of EUR 2,771 (still flagged as to be confirmed) and pays visa, residence permit, health and liability insurance, so you must still self-fund roughly EUR 2,500-3,500 per month of living and study costs in Nijmegen. The scholarship is applied for inside your Master's admission application in OSIRIS, with submission by 31 January 2027 and a complete file by 14 February 2027 - an incomplete file is not reviewed at all. Only 26 awards exist across six faculties, and your odds depend heavily on which faculty you target (Science alone holds 9). Remember that admission to the programme and selection for the scholarship are separate decisions, so one can succeed without the other.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong non-EEA applicants with an excellent, relevant Bachelor's degree from outside the Netherlands who are admitted to an English-taught Radboud Master's and can independently finance living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Sit an accepted English test early or confirm your exemption, so the certificate can be uploaded before the 14 February 2027 cut-off rather than the 31 January submission date.
Brief your two referees now and ask for academic references that follow Radboud's published reference letter guidelines.
Write a programme-specific motivation letter - faculty committees score its quality and relevance directly.
Open the tuition page of your target programme for 2027/2028 so you know the exact non-EEA fee the reduction is worth against.
Budget the non-refundable EUR 100 application fee and about EUR 2,500-3,500 per month of living costs the award does not cover.
Submit in OSIRIS well before 31 January 2027 so there is room to answer the admissions check-back and replace missing or illegible documents.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting on or near 31 January and then missing the 14 February completeness deadline - incomplete applications are excluded from selection without review.
Reference letters that ignore the university's guidelines or come from non-academic referees, when two academic references are preferred.
A generic motivation letter, since ambition and the relevance of the letter are scored criteria.
Applying through an Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree Master's, which are excluded despite being English-taught.
Assuming that admission to the programme implies the scholarship, or expecting living-cost support the award explicitly does not provide.
Targeting an oversubscribed faculty - with 26 awards across six faculties, some faculties have only 1-2 places.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living and study costs in the Netherlands are not covered: Radboud's official student budget for non-EU/EEA students totals about EUR 2,523-3,504 per month (accommodation EUR 561-600, tuition EUR 231-2,093, books and materials EUR 53, insurance EUR 55-133, transport EUR 72, groceries EUR 244, leisure, clothing, subscriptions and contingencies), plus a non-refundable EUR 100 application fee. Grant holders themselves pay the reduced EUR 2,771 tuition fee.
document_audit: Reference letters must follow Radboud's published reference letter guidelines; two academic referees are preferred.

Documents uploaded for the admission application may be reused for the scholarship, but only if legible and correct - anything missing, illegible or incorrect is sent back for resubmission and can burn your 14 February window.
Proof of English proficiency should be in the file before 14 February 2027, not merely before the initial submission.

You need full admission to an English-taught Master's starting 1 September 2027 as stated in the formal letter of admission - the award cannot be carried into a Pre-Master's, a part-time route or another institution.
alerts: Two clocks run in this round: OSIRIS submission by 31 January 2027 23:59 CET and a complete application by 14 February 2027 23:59 CET, with decisions notified before mid-April 2027 (date subject to change).
The EUR 2,771 reduced fee is explicitly labelled 'amount to be confirmed' on the official page, so treat the final figure as provisional.
In a two-year Master's you must pass all courses in the first year to qualify for the grant again in the second year - a failed course can cost you year two.
The Radboud Scholarship can be combined with the NL Scholarship, so check whether that additional partial funding applies to you before assuming this award is your only source.
Holding a non-EEA passport is not enough on its own: you must also not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: File the Master's admission application in OSIRIS with the Radboud Scholarship option ticked before 31 January 2027, respond immediately to any admissions check-back, and have all documents complete by 14 February 2027; faculty selection committees then assess the file and Student Life and International Mobility informs applicants of the decision before mid-April 2027.
